scope: One source sweep from each of the existing 24 development cards; not all 374 sweeps. Existing pack predates semantic repairs.
regions: Candidate regions are hypotheses for diagnostic counts only. Bounds are half-open [ray_min,ray_max,gate_min,gate_max], native array indices. They are not submitted labels or accuracy denominators.

notes.observations: Distinct high-RHOHV/SQIH echo structures at gates roughly 80–240, rays 100–280, support probable weather. Near-range strong returns and near-zero velocities remain mixed/uncertain. Diffuse far-range low-quality speckle is background-like.
notes.additional: Check adjacent scans/elevations; inspect near-range static removals separately.

notes.observations: Smooth range-dependent SP reflectivity extends across low-RHOHV/low-SQIH, noisy-velocity gates. Embedded higher-quality structures remain; broad spatial smoothness alone would wrongly protect much of the background-like field.
notes.additional: Verify receiver calibration and compare embedded structure across scans before labelling noise as truth.

notes.observations: Higher-quality patches near gates 35–70 and around gates 140–220 contrast with widespread low-quality speckle. Weather is plausible; near-range and small features remain uncertain without temporal context.
notes.additional: Inspect retention of near-range high-quality patches; preserve potential biology/mixed echoes.

notes.observations: SP background-like smooth reflectivity has predominantly low quality and noisy velocity. Isolated coherent high-quality patches near ray 340/gate 75 and ray 175/gate 40 should be retained.
notes.additional: Check receiver-floor model and weak-patch continuity; small area alone is not an artefact label.

notes.observations: Large connected high-RHOHV structures at multiple ranges, with matching SQIH and velocity organisation, support probable precipitation. Near-range bright stationary returns and far-range fringes remain ambiguous.
notes.additional: Check retained weather structure and uncertain boundary gates separately.

notes.observations: Almost entirely smooth range-dependent reflectivity, low RHOHV/SQIH and noisy velocity; no clear coherent weather feature in this sweep. Thin ray discontinuities are visible. This is a strong receiver-background stress case, subject to calibration confirmation.
notes.additional: Verify instrument noise calibration. Measure retention of this region, without treating visual assessment as independent truth.

notes.observations: Connected moderate-reflectivity echo at gates roughly 50–200 and rays 40–170 has coherent velocity and elevated RHOHV/SQIH. Widespread distant low-quality speckle is distinct.
notes.additional: Inspect weak edges and the narrow near-range uncertain strip.

notes.observations: Broad high-quality echo has a coherent velocity field, with embedded low-quality gaps at larger ranges. Strong useful-echo retention test; a smooth DBZH floor also fills gaps and must not count as weather continuity.
notes.additional: Compare the quality-defined gaps with retained background and preserve the connected weather regions.

notes.observations: Most distant gates are low-quality speckle. Near-range coherent structures and a few small higher-RHOHV spots exist, but target identity is uncertain in this single 3-degree sweep.
notes.additional: Use adjacent elevations/time and terrain context; do not classify the near-range echo as clutter or biology from this panel alone.

notes.observations: Far-range feature at gates roughly 145–185/rays 175–240 has elevated RHOHV and coherent inbound velocity, supporting probable weather. Strong near-range nearly stationary returns require clutter/mixed adjudication.
notes.additional: Retain far weather; inspect static-map behaviour near the radar.

notes.observations: Several narrow high-quality weather-like structures coexist with a broad near-range lower-RHOHV echo and background-like speckle. Narrow ray features also need interference checks. Biology cannot be separated confidently from the near-range mixture here.
notes.additional: Preserve ambiguous near-range returns and check temporal/azimuthal persistence before assigning artefact labels.

notes.observations: Strong weather-like core around gates 40–90/rays 60–120 has high RHOHV and organised positive radial velocity. A smaller coherent patch occurs near ray 320/gate 80; smooth low-quality background fills remaining range.
notes.additional: Use core retention as a development check, keeping weak edges and background separate.

notes.observations: Connected high-RHOHV weather-like core at gates roughly 60–150/rays 175–245, with further bands near ray 330. Weak outer echo and near-range mixed returns need separate treatment.
notes.additional: Check main-core retention and avoid classifying every narrow band as interference.

notes.observations: Near-range strong/smooth velocity returns and high SQIH have variable RHOHV and ZDR. The near-range target mixture is uncertain; a small distant high-quality band is visible around ray 280.
notes.additional: Require terrain, temporal persistence and adjacent elevations before identifying ground clutter or biology.

notes.observations: Bright near-range returns with almost stationary velocity are consistent with clutter but may contain mixed useful signal. The weak distant patch at gates 220–300/rays 0–55 is coherent across several fields and needs retention scrutiny.
notes.additional: Preserve the weak patch pending temporal/elevation evidence; this case had previous candidate-metric exposure.

notes.observations: Complex near-range echo coexists with coherent high-RHOHV weather-like features near ray 240/gates 150–220 and ray 330 at long range. Narrow full-range lines also require detector-specific inspection.
notes.additional: Separate coherent weather, near-clutter mixtures and possible narrow interference; no taxonomy can be assigned.

notes.observations: Strong narrow ray features and near-range returns coexist with weaker curved outer structures. Some linear features have elevated RHOHV/SQIH, so line shape or high correlation alone cannot settle weather versus interference/clutter.
notes.additional: Inspect detector-specific response and temporal persistence; do not automatically delete every radial structure.

notes.observations: Compact high-RHOHV/SQIH weather-like patches at gates roughly 55–100/rays 280–350 and around ray 165 are embedded in widespread low-quality speckle.
notes.additional: Test retention of compact echoes and their weak edges; small connected area is insufficient removal evidence.

notes.observations: Extensive connected high-RHOHV precipitation-like echo and coherent velocity at near to middle ranges. Low-quality gaps and far-field speckle are separable; strong near-range returns can still contain clutter.
notes.additional: Inspect static-rule removals within connected weather and quantify background separately.

notes.observations: A relatively weak connected echo around gates 130–260/rays 140–240 is supported by elevated RHOHV/SQIH and organised velocity; the surroundings are low-quality speckle. Near-range narrow returns remain uncertain.
notes.additional: This is a useful weak-echo retention test. Inspect edges and removed gates before concluding damage.

notes.observations: Smooth range-dependent reflectivity fills almost the entire sweep despite low RHOHV/SQIH and noisy velocity. Tiny isolated enhanced-quality returns and narrow ray discontinuities remain uncertain.
notes.additional: Confirm the receiver/background model and retain isolated uncertain features pending adjacent-scan evidence.

notes.observations: Far-range low-quality speckle dominates. A very narrow full-range feature near ray 214 has enhanced RHOHV but weak SQIH; its identity needs independent interference and temporal checks.
notes.additional: Use the off-feature far-range region as a development background stress test. Do not classify the radial feature from shape alone.

notes.observations: High-RHOHV weather-like bands at rays roughly 210–270/gates 100–190 and farther ranges coexist with bright near-range mixed returns. The source moments support retaining the connected outer echo.
notes.additional: Inspect near-range static removals separately from the probable weather; confirm with adjacent volumes.

notes.observations: A large connected high-RHOHV feature at gates roughly 140–280/rays 160–245 has organised velocity and moderate SQIH. Bright near-range almost stationary returns remain clutter/mixed candidates.
notes.additional: Check the interior probable-weather region and near-range mixtures separately; source-only visual interpretation is not independent truth.
